title: Transfer of fppf source locality from schemes to algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and let $P$ be an isomorphism-invariant property of morphisms of $S$-schemes. Suppose $P$ is etale local on source-and-target in the sense explicitly defined in [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion], and let $P_{\mathrm{sp}}$ be its extension to morphisms of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] by the equivalent etale presentation conditions of that node. Suppose that for every scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ and every fppf covering $\{q_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ [def-pc-fppf-site], one has $P(f)$ if and only if $P(fq_i)$ for every $i$. Then for every morphism of algebraic spaces $g:A\to B$ and every fppf covering $\{a_j:A_j\to A\}_{j\in J}$ one has $P_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)$ if and only if $P_{\mathrm{sp}}(ga_j)$ for every $j$. Here an fppf covering of algebraic spaces is a set-indexed jointly surjective family of maps flat and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; jointly surjective means surjective on field-valued point classes [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family]. The empty family is allowed over the empty space. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 06ER (lemma-transfer-from-schemes), specialized to the fppf topology; spaces-topologies.tex Tag 03Y9 (lemma-fppf) supplies covering calculus.

proof.text: Fix $g:A\to B$ and the fppf family $\{a_j:A_j\to A\}$. The presentation criterion gives schemes $U,V$, representable etale maps $a:U\to A$, $b:V\to B$, and $h:U\to V$, with $a$ surjective and $ga=bh$. Put $W_j=A_j\times_A U$. The fibre-product lemma makes $W_j$ an algebraic space and $p_j:W_j\to A_j$ surjective etale, by pulling back the singleton etale cover $\{a\}$. Choose a scheme atlas $e_j:U_j\to W_j$ surjective etale from the definition of algebraic space. Write $q_j:U_j\to U$ for the other projection composed with $e_j$.

source.place: Tag 06ER (lemma-transfer-from-schemes), first paragraph; use the presentation-existence clause of Tag 03MJ

proof.text: The composite $t_j=p_je_j:U_j\to A_j$ is representable surjective etale. Explicitly, on a scheme $T\to A_j$ let $D=T\times_{A_j}W_j$, a scheme surjective etale over $T$. Then $E=D\times_{W_j}U_j$ is a scheme surjective etale over $D$. On test schemes, compatible pairs identify $E$ with $T\times_{A_j}U_j$, so the scheme covering-composition lemma makes its projection to $T$ surjective etale. This verifies the representable scheme tests for $t_j$ without treating $A_j$ or $W_j$ as schemes. The pullback relation gives $ga_jt_j=bhq_j$.

source.place: Tag 06ER (lemma-transfer-from-schemes), first and last paragraphs; representable composition expanded on scheme tests

proof.text: By covering calculus (2), $\{W_j\to U\}_j$ is fppf. Each singleton $\{e_j:U_j\to W_j\}$ is fppf by (1); composing these covers by (3) gives $\{q_j:U_j\to U\}_j$ fppf as a family of spaces. Clause (4) makes it an fppf covering of schemes, since $U$ and every $U_j$ are schemes. The assumed scheme source locality applied to $h:U\to V$ and this covering gives $P(h)\Longleftrightarrow(\forall j,\ P(hq_j))$.

source.place: Tag 06ER (lemma-transfer-from-schemes), second paragraph and middle equivalence; Tag 03Y9 (lemma-fppf), parts (2),(3)

proof.text: The presentation $(a,b,h)$ has surjective source map, so the presentation criterion gives $P_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)\Longleftrightarrow P(h)$. For every $j$, the diagram $(t_j,b,hq_j)$ is a presentation of $ga_j$ with surjective source map by step 2; the same criterion gives $P(hq_j)\Longleftrightarrow P_{\mathrm{sp}}(ga_j)$. Substitution into the equivalence of step 3 proves both directions of the assertion. No surjectivity of $b$ is needed by the criterion. If the covering family is empty, $A$ and hence $U$ are empty; step 3 uses exactly the empty scheme covering allowed in the scheme-locality hypothesis and proves $P(h)$ from the empty conjunction, so the argument still applies.
